label: Gamescope
description: Run the game in a window of its own, at the resolution and refresh rate below; a launcher already inside gamescope puts it on that one instead.

label: Resolution
description: What the game renders at; auto is the screen's own. A lower one is upscaled to the screen, lighter on the GPU.

label: Refresh rate
description: The refresh rate the game sees; auto is the screen's own.

label: Adaptive sync
description: Variable refresh rate (FreeSync, G-Sync) when the screen supports it: no tearing, no stutter below the refresh rate.

label: Show MangoHud
description: Draw the overlay (frame rate, frame time, GPU and CPU load) over the game from launch; off keeps MangoHud loaded but hidden, the frame rate limit still holds, and the in-game menu or the pad macro shows it mid-game and writes the state back here.

label: Frame rate limit
description: MangoHud holds the game to this many frames per second, overlay or not; auto is the refresh rate the game sees, and no limit for an emulator, which paces itself.

label: Pause on HOME
description: Freeze the game while the launcher covers it, so the pad drives the menu alone; it runs again on Resume. Off for a game that must keep running (online play).

label: Scaler
description: How a smaller picture fills the screen: integer keeps pixels whole, fit keeps the aspect, fill and stretch do not.

label: Filter
description: The upscaling filter: fsr and nis sharpen, nearest and pixel keep pixel art crisp.

label: Sharpness
description: For fsr and nis: 0 is sharpest, 20 softest.

label: Gamescope arguments
description: Extra gamescope flags, after and over the fields above.

label: Environment variables
description: Environment variables for the game; a game's win over the global ones.

label: Wrapper command
description: A command the game runs through, innermost: gamemoderun, taskset -c 0-7…

label: Arguments
description: Arguments appended to the game's command line.

label: Working directory
description: The folder the game starts in.

label: Before the game
description: A shell line run before the game starts.

label: After the game
description: A shell line run once the game has ended.

label: Proton build
description: The Proton build umu-run starts the game with.

label: Wayland
description: Proton's own Wayland driver instead of Xwayland: lower latency, proper scaling; dropped inside gamescope unless it exposes Wayland.

label: HDR
description: HDR output on an HDR screen: Proton's PROTON_ENABLE_HDR, and --hdr-enabled on gamescope.

label: Wine prefix
description: The Wine prefix the game runs in; empty: <prefixes_root>/<id>.

label: Architecture
description: WINEARCH for a plain Wine prefix.

label: umu id
description: GAMEID for umu-run's protonfixes; empty: umu-default.

label: Store
description: STORE for umu-run's protonfixes.

label: DLL overrides
description: WINEDLLOVERRIDES, one key per DLL without .dll: d3d11 = "n,b".

label: Esync
description: Faster thread synchronisation through eventfd; on for most games, off if one hangs or stutters.

label: Fsync
description: Faster still, through the kernel's futex2; takes over from esync when the kernel has it.

label: NTSync
description: The kernel's NT synchronisation driver, the fastest; needs Linux 6.14 and a Proton built for it, else falls back.

label: DLSS upgrade
description: Games with DLSS use the newest DLSS from the NVIDIA driver instead of the one they ship. NVIDIA GeForce RTX only.

label: FSR 4 upgrade
description: Games with FSR 3.1 use FSR 4 instead, sharper and cleaner. Radeon RX 9000 (RDNA 4), or RX 7000 (RDNA 3) at a cost, through Proton's RDNA 3 variant picked for it.

label: XeSS upgrade
description: Games with XeSS use the newest XeSS instead of the one they ship. Any GPU; best on Intel Arc.

label: OptiScaler
description: Adds FSR 4 or XeSS to games that only offer DLSS, through OptiScaler. For AMD and Intel; needs a Proton that ships it (CachyOS, GE).

label: Gamescope program
description: The gamescope binary: a name on PATH or a path.

label: umu-run program
description: The umu-run binary: a name on PATH or a path.
